content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The MINCOMMIT rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

- **§ 3(a)** — compensation is strictly **time-and-materials** per Statement of Work, i.e. fees for ordered services only.
- **§ 1(a)** — Contractor is retained **"on a task by task basis,"** with scope arising only from mutually agreed SOWs.
- **§ 6(a)** — either party may terminate **for any or no reason on 15 days' notice** when no SOW is outstanding, so there is no lock-in even in principle.

A full-text search for *minimum, commit, shortfall, retainer, take or pay, volume* returned only unrelated hits (exclusive-property/licence language in § 4 and the entire-agreement clause in § 7). No commitment exists that would need reducing or true-up treatment.

One item flagged in the rationale for context but deliberately **not** treated as a deviation here: § 3(b) allows Contractor to change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap. That is a price-escalation concern rather than a volume commitment, and raising it under MINCOMMIT would double-count a term properly owned by a price-increase rule.
